# `codec2_3200` test fixtures

Reference data for cross-validating `src/codec2_3200/`'s independent Rust
implementation against the real Codec2-mod C reference (see
`src/codec2_3200/mod.rs`'s own module doc comment for why this is an
independent implementation rather than a port). Captured with a small
instrumentation patch (`-DCODEC2_INSTRUMENT`, not part of Codec2-mod's own
real source) added to a local build of `vendor/codec2-mod/`, which logs
real intermediate values -- `R[]`, `ak[]`, `P[]`/`Q[]`, `lsp[]`, encoder-side
energy -- at specific call sites, one line per real analysis frame.

## What's committed, and why

- `codec2_r_dump.txt`, `codec2_ak_dump.txt`, `codec2_pq_dump.txt`,
  `codec2_lsp_dump.txt`, `codec2_enc_e_dump.txt`: derived from running the
  real reference against five local 8kHz WAV files (filenames
  `brian_g8sez.wav`, `david_vk5dgr.wav`, `k0pfx_mel.wav`, `mooneer.wav`,
  `peter.wav`) whose names match the callsigns of the Codec2/FreeDV
  project's own leadership team (David Rowe VK5DGR, Mooneer Salem K6AQ,
  Mel Whitten K0PFX, Brian Morrison G8SEZ, Peter Marks VK3TPM) -- their
  own donated voice samples, used elsewhere in that project's own testing
  (checked: not literally `raw/` in `drowe67/codec2`'s own repo, which
  uses a different, unnamed sample set -- reviewed and confirmed fine by
  Bruce, who knows the team: samples of team members who wouldn't
  restrict their own donated samples to the project's own detriment).
  What's actually committed here holds only *abstracted numeric analysis
  features* (LPC coefficients, Chebyshev polynomial coefficients, LSP
  frequencies in radians, a single energy scalar per frame) -- not audio
  waveform data, and not byte-recoverable back into speech, which was the
  original reasoning for treating this as lower-risk than the
  waveform-adjacent `Wn[]` data below even before that confirmation.
  Subsampled (every 7th frame) from a larger local capture to keep the
  fixture small; frame indices are not meaningful outside this file.
- `codec2_bits_dump.txt`: same five real-speech WAVs, same subsampling,
  but one line per `codec2_encode()` call (not per `speech_to_uq_lsps()`
  call, so its own indexing doesn't line up with the files above): the
  two `voiced` bits, `Wo`/energy/LSP-delta indices, and the real *packed*
  `bits[0..7]` those indices produced -- used by
  `bits::tests::pack_frame_matches_the_real_reference_bits_on_real_captured_field_values`
  to check this crate's own bit-packing/Gray-coding bit-exactly against
  the reference's real output. Numeric indices and packed bytes, same
  "abstracted, not audio" reasoning as the files above.
- `synthetic_codec2_wn_dump.txt`, `synthetic_codec2_r_dump.txt`: the
  reference's real windowed analysis buffer (`Wn[]`, which *is*
  essentially audio-domain data -- real samples, just multiplied by a Hann
  window) and its corresponding `R[]`, but captured from a locally
  synthesized, non-speech test signal (swept sinusoids plus a little
  deterministic pseudo-noise, generated by a short Python script, not
  checked in) instead of anyone's real recorded voice. Used only by
  `lpc::tests::autocorrelate_matches_the_real_reference_r_on_a_synthetic_signals_real_captured_wn_data`
  to cross-check `window.rs`'s normalization scale against the reference.
- `synthetic_c_encoded_bits.bin`, `synthetic_c_decoded_pcm.bin`: the same
  synthesized non-speech signal above, this time run through the real
  reference's own full `codec2_encode`/`codec2_decode` round trip --
  `synthetic_c_encoded_bits.bin` is 200 real packed frames (raw bytes,
  `BYTES_PER_FRAME` each, back-to-back), `synthetic_c_decoded_pcm.bin` is
  the real reference decoder's own real PCM output for them (raw
  little-endian i16, no WAV header). Used by
  `codec2_3200::tests::decoder_matches_the_real_reference_decoder_on_a_real_captured_synthetic_signal_bitstream`
  to check `Decoder`'s real output against the real reference decoder's
  own, automatically and reproducibly (this crate's own synthesis PRNG
  is deterministically seeded). Deliberately *not* the real donated
  speech WAVs for this one: unlike the scalar-feature files above, this
  fixture's whole point is real reconstructed *audio*, and even lossily
  vocoded, the real reference decoder's own PCM output of real donated
  speech is still recognizable speech -- the same line this README
  already draws against real `Wn[]`/`Sn[]` data, just on the decode
  side. The synthetic signal has no such concern.

Deliberately **not** committed: any dump of real `Wn[]`/`Sn[]` (actual
speech waveform samples), or real decoded PCM audio, from the real
donated voice recordings above -- unlike the scalar features, both are
audio-domain data close enough to the original recordings to warrant the
same caution `tests/fixtures/`'s own `.gitignore` entry already applies
to the real off-air WSPR recording used elsewhere in this crate.

## Regenerating

The instrumentation patch and capture script aren't checked in (they lived
in a session scratchpad). To recapture the `codec2_*_dump.txt`/
`synthetic_codec2_*_dump.txt` files: add `INSTR_DUMP_*` calls (see
`inc/instrument.h`'s existing macros for the pattern) at the relevant call
sites in a local `vendor/codec2-mod/` checkout, build with
`-DCODEC2_INSTRUMENT`, and run against real speech (any 8kHz mono WAV) for
the five real-speech-derived files, or a synthesized non-speech signal for
the `synthetic_codec2_*` files.

To recapture `synthetic_c_encoded_bits.bin`/`synthetic_c_decoded_pcm.bin`:
no instrumentation needed, just the real reference's own unmodified
`codec2_encode`/`codec2_decode` -- encode the same synthesized non-speech
signal to get the bits, decode those bits to get the PCM, strip any WAV
header from the PCM output.

## Reference-encoder bitstreams of real speech (added 2026-11-06)

`osr_0010_codec2mod_c_encoded_bits.bin`, `osr_0011_...`, `osr_0030_...`, `osr_0031_...`: the Codec2-mod C
encoder's own 3200 bit/s bitstream (8 bytes per 20 ms frame, nothing else) for the four Open Speech Repository
sentences in `../osr_speech` (the WAV's samples, whole frames only). Produced on 2026-11-06 with
M17-Project/Codec2-mod commit `7c334283794fa6304dc014f12df70afc8393143a` (2026-09-30, `main`), built for
x86-64 with gcc 13.3 `-O2` against glibc 2.39, driven by a 20-line program that calls
`codec2_encoder_init` once and `codec2_encode` per frame. The vendored January commit
(`vendor/codec2-mod`, `680a0b1`) produces byte-identical files (checked), which is Codec2-mod's own
bit-exactness claim for its September refactor. SHA-256:

| File | SHA-256 |
|---|---|
| `osr_0010_codec2mod_c_encoded_bits.bin` | `b8994e36e40f0c3e50697e550129e55c222572f9e57c3221a5e1104841d43e11` |
| `osr_0011_codec2mod_c_encoded_bits.bin` | `94a68af414c6155116a4a29ac7f44a72a9db1aa9d6be719b18bf87e98761699c` |
| `osr_0030_codec2mod_c_encoded_bits.bin` | `0aeafad993f9d63abe138d0b1226469dfdfcb2ab63686157bcf8571ce3be71d7` |
| `osr_0031_codec2mod_c_encoded_bits.bin` | `202a6f4acbdca839d43aaacb433a51941c3fbba6ce3b951078e00f09d366466d` |

They are the output of a program, not its code, and carry the same OSR attribution as the speech
(`../osr_speech/README.md`). Used by `tests/codec2_3200_encoder_vs_reference.rs`.
